memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now kill all the boys. And kill every woman who has slept with a man, but save for yourselves every girl who has never slept with a man. All of you who have killed anyone or touched anyone who was killed must stay outside the camp seven days. On the third and seventh days you must purify yourselves and your captives." - Num 31:17-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are among the hardest words in the Old Testament, and we do them no honour by softening them. We must be honest: this is a severe, God-directed act of judgment on a nation at a particular moment in history, tied to the Peor rebellion that had nearly destroyed Israel from within. It is not a general command, not a model for warfare today, and certainly not a pattern the church is ever called to follow. Jesus explicitly refused to let His disciples call down destruction on others (Luke 9:54-56).

Passages like this remind us that God is holy and that sin, left unchecked, spreads like a plague. They also remind us that the old covenant operated under a system of judgment that pointed forward to something better. The writer of Hebrews tells us these things were shadows, and that in Christ God has spoken a final and fuller word (Heb 1:1-2). We read the shadows in light of the substance.

Even here, notice the concern for purification — those who touched death had to be cleansed. Sin and death always require cleansing. And the wonderful truth of the gospel is that Jesus provides a cleansing no ritual ever could. His blood makes the guilty clean and gives life to those who were under the sentence of death (Heb 9:14). We bring our hardest questions to the foot of His cross.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you respond when Scripture confronts you with something you find difficult?
2. Why is it important not to soften or explain away God's holiness?
3. How does the cleansing Christ offers speak into this passage's theme?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Lord, some of Your ways are beyond me, yet I trust that You are always just and good. Thank You that in Christ I am cleansed and given life. Help me hold hard truths with a humble and trusting heart. Amen.
